info.name: Tutoring Platform API
info.description:
# Atlas — Tutoring Platform API

Backend for a coding-education platform: courses → chapters → lectures → exercises, with Google OAuth2 login, role-based access (admin/student), enrollment-gated content, and remote code execution with test-case grading for exercise submissions.

## Getting started
1. Set `base_url` (defaults to `http://localhost:8000/api/v1`)
2. Open the **Google Login** URL in a browser and sign in
3. Copy the `code` from the redirect into `google_code`, then run **Google Callback** — your `access_token` is saved automatically
4. Every other request authenticates using `{{access_token}}` automatically

## Roles
- **admin** — full CRUD on all content (courses, chapters, lectures, exercises, blocks, test cases)
- **professor** — read-only access to courses they are assigned to (via `POST /courses/{id}/professors`). Assigned by admins.
- **student** — read-only, and only for courses they're enrolled in. Must `POST /enrollments` before accessing course content.

## Code execution & grading
Student submissions are executed remotely on an isolated Docker container. If an exercise has test cases, the submitted code is run **one test case at a time** (sequentially), feeding each test case's `input` as stdin. Execution **stops immediately on the first failure** — no further test cases are run after a wrong answer, crash, or timeout. Each submission returns `passed_count` and `total_count` as integers (e.g. `17` and `36`, display as `"17/36"`) alongside a `test_results` array with the per-test-case breakdown. `passed_count`/`total_count` are `null` if the exercise has no test cases.

## Folder guide
| Folder | Covers |
|---|---|
| Auth | Google OAuth2 login/logout, JWT issuance |
| Courses | Top-level content containers |
| Enrollments | Connects students to courses — required before content access |
| Professors | Assigns professor-role users to courses — admin only |
| Availability | Professor-published time windows with student capacity caps |
| Bookings | Student session bookings within availability windows |
| Chapters | Ordered groups of lectures within a course |
| Lectures | Markdown content blocks + exercises within a chapter |
| Exercises | Coding problems with a starter `code_template` and test cases used for grading |
| Submissions | Student code submissions, executed remotely in Docker, graded against test cases |

Each folder has its own detailed documentation with multiple worked examples — click into a folder and view its description.

item.description:
## Auth — Google OAuth2 Login

Handles sign-in via Google and issues a JWT used to authenticate every other request in this collection.

**Flow:**
1. Open `Google Login` in a browser (not Postman — Google's consent screen can't be completed inside Postman)
2. After consenting, Google redirects to the callback URL with a `code` query param
3. Copy that `code` into the `google_code` collection variable
4. Run `Google Callback` in Postman — this exchanges the code for a JWT and upserts the user in the database
5. The JWT is auto-saved to `{{access_token}}` via a test script — every other request in this collection uses it automatically

---

### Example 1 — First-time login (new user)
**Request:** `GET /auth/google/callback?code=4/0Adk...`
**Response `200`:**
```json
{
  "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...",
  "token_type": "bearer",
  "user": {
    "id": "91deb5e7-464a-471f-9fb7-f4589ce0f35d",
    "name": "Octavian Cazan",
    "email": "o.cazatavian@gmail.com",
    "role": "student",
    "created_at": "2026-06-20T10:15:00Z"
  }
}
```
A new row is created in `users` with `role = student` by default.

### Example 2 — Returning user
Same request, same flow — but instead of creating a new user, the existing row is matched by email and a fresh JWT is issued. The `user.id` stays identical across logins.

### Example 3 — Logout
**Request:** `POST /auth/logout` (with `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}`)
**Response `200`:**
```json
{ "message": "Successfully logged out. Discard your token." }
```
JWTs are stateless, so this just signals intent — the actual logout is the client discarding `{{access_token}}`.

item.name: Courses

request.description: List the course catalogue. Filters: q (title search), professor_id. include=stats adds chapter/lecture/exercise/enrolled/professor/submission counts. envelope=1 returns {items,total,skip,limit}.
Transactionally set every course's position from the ordered id list (admin). 204 on success.
Reorder the chapters within a course (admin). 204 on success.

item.description:
## Courses

Top-level content container. A course holds chapters, which hold lectures, which hold blocks and exercises.

**Access control:**
| Action | Admin | Enrolled student | Unenrolled student |
|---|---|---|---|
| Browse catalogue (`GET /courses`) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| View a specific course (`GET /courses/{id}`) | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ 403 |
| Create / update / delete | ✓ | ✗ 403 | ✗ 403 |

The catalogue list is open to any authenticated user so students can browse before enrolling. Everything keyed to a specific `course_id` requires enrollment.

---

### Example 1 — Admin creates a course
**Request:** `POST /courses`
```json
{ "title": "Introduction to Python", "description": "A beginner-friendly Python course." }
```
**Response `201`:**
```json
{
  "id": "018732f6-ae85-4cfc-ba46-e3e78a4291d8",
  "title": "Introduction to Python",
  "description": "A beginner-friendly Python course.",
  "created_at": "2026-06-20T10:00:00Z"
}
```

### Example 2 — Student browses the catalogue, then tries to open one
`GET /courses` → returns all courses regardless of enrollment.
`GET /courses/018732f6-.../detail` on a course the student is **not** enrolled in:
**Response `403`:**
```json
{ "detail": "You are not enrolled in this course" }
```
The student must call `POST /enrollments` first (see the Enrollments folder).

### Example 3 — Get full course tree
**Request:** `GET /courses/{{course_id}}/detail`
Returns the course with `chapters → lectures → blocks/exercises` fully nested in one call — useful for rendering an entire course page without N+1 requests.

item.name: Enrollments

request.description: Admins see all enrollments (filter by user_id/course_id); students see their own. expand=course,user embeds summaries. envelope=1 returns {items,total,skip,limit}.
Returns the current student's enrollments.
Admins can enroll any user. Students can only enroll themselves (user_id must match their own id).
Admins can unenroll anyone. Students can only unenroll themselves.

item.description:
## Enrollments

Connects students to courses. Enrollment is the gate that the `enrolled_for_*` dependencies check before letting a student see chapter/lecture/exercise content.

**Rules:**
- Admins can enroll or unenroll **any** user in **any** course.
- Students can only enroll/unenroll **themselves** (`user_id` in the body must match their own JWT `sub`).
- Re-enrolling in the same course returns `409 Conflict` (the `UNIQUE(user_id, course_id)` DB constraint).

---

### Example 1 — Student self-enrolls
**Request:** `POST /enrollments`
```json
{ "user_id": "{{user_id}}", "course_id": "{{course_id}}" }
```
**Response `201`:**
```json
{
  "id": "a1b2c3d4-...",
  "user_id": "91deb5e7-464a-471f-9fb7-f4589ce0f35d",
  "course_id": "018732f6-ae85-4cfc-ba46-e3e78a4291d8",
  "enrolled_at": "2026-06-23T09:00:00Z"
}
```

### Example 2 — Student tries to enroll someone else
**Request:** `POST /enrollments` with a `user_id` that isn't their own.
**Response `403`:**
```json
{ "detail": "Students can only enroll themselves" }
```

### Example 3 — Duplicate enrollment
Calling the same `POST /enrollments` twice with identical `user_id`/`course_id`:
**Response `409`:**
```json
{ "detail": "User is already enrolled in this course" }
```

### Example 4 — Checking your own enrollments
**Request:** `GET /enrollments/me`
**Response `200`:**
```json
[
  { "id": "a1b2c3d4-...", "user_id": "91deb5e7-...", "course_id": "018732f6-...", "enrolled_at": "2026-06-23T09:00:00Z" }
]
```

item.name: Professors

request.description: Assign a professor-role user to a course. Admin only. Returns 400 if the user is not a professor, 409 if already assigned.
List professors assigned to a course. Each item now embeds the professor's profile under `user` {id, name, email} (item #7).
Remove a professor's assignment from a course. Admin only. Returns 404 if the assignment does not exist.

item.description:
## Professors

Assigns users with the `professor` role to courses. A course can have multiple professors; a professor can be assigned to multiple courses.

**Rules:**
- Only admins can assign or remove professors.
- The user must have `role: professor` before being assigned — use the debug token or update the user role first.
- Professors access course content through the same `enrolled_for_*` guards as students, but via `course_assignments` instead of `enrollments`.

---

### Assign a professor
**Request:** `POST /courses/{{course_id}}/professors`
```json
{ "user_id": "{{user_id}}" }
```
**Response `201`:**
```json
{ "id": "...", "user_id": "...", "course_id": "...", "assigned_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z" }
```

### Remove a professor
**Request:** `DELETE /courses/{{course_id}}/professors/{{user_id}}`
**Response `204`:** No content.

item.name: Students

request.description: List students. Admins see all students; professors see only students enrolled in courses they are assigned to. Returns each student's id, name, email, role, and created_at.

Retrieve a single student's data by id. Admins can retrieve any student; professors can only retrieve students enrolled in a course they are assigned to. Returns 404 if the id does not belong to an accessible student.
Submission feed scoped to one student (admin, or professor for their courses).
Per-exercise best status and attempt count for one student (solved/attempted/not-started matrix).

item.description:
## Students

Read-only access to student user records. A student is a `User` with `role: student`.

**Rules:**
- Admins see all students.
- Professors see only students enrolled in courses they are assigned to (via `course_assignments`). A student is visible to a professor if the student has an enrollment in any course the professor is assigned to.
- Students have no access.

---

### List students
**Request:** `GET /students`
**Response `200`:**
```json
[
  { "id": "...", "name": "Jane Doe", "email": "jane@example.com", "role": "student", "created_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z" }
]
```

### Get a student
**Request:** `GET /students/{{student_id}}`
**Response `200`:**
```json
{ "id": "...", "name": "Jane Doe", "email": "jane@example.com", "role": "student", "created_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z" }
```
**Response `404`:** Student not found or not accessible to you.

item.name: Availability

request.description: Professor creates an availability window for a course they are assigned to. `max_students` caps how many students can book into this window.
Returns windows scoped by role. Professors see their own; students see windows for their enrolled courses; admins see all. Each window includes `booked_count` so clients can show remaining capacity.
Professor updates their own window. All fields optional. Admins can update any window.
Professor deletes their own window. Cascades to all bookings within it. Admins can delete any window.

item.description:
## Availability

Professors publish time windows during which they are available to teach. Each window is scoped to a specific course and carries a `max_students` cap.

**Rules:**
- Only professors (and admins) can create, update, or delete windows.
- A professor can only manage windows they own.
- Deleting a window cascades to all bookings inside it.
- `booked_count` in the response is the number of active (non-cancelled) bookings against that window.

---

### Example — create a window
```json
POST /availability
{
  "course_id": "{{course_id}}",
  "start_time": "2026-09-01T10:00:00Z",
  "end_time":   "2026-09-01T12:00:00Z",
  "max_students": 3
}
```
**Response `201`:**
```json
{ "id": "...", "professor_id": "...", "course_id": "...", "start_time": "...", "end_time": "...", "max_students": 3, "booked_count": 0, "created_at": "..." }
```

item.name: Bookings

request.description: Student books a time slot within a professor's availability window. Returns 403 if not enrolled in the course, 422 if times fall outside the window, 409 if the window is fully booked.
Returns bookings scoped by role: students see their own, professors see bookings on their windows, admins see all.
Update booking status. Professor can set `confirmed` or `cancelled`. Student can only set `cancelled`. Admin has no restrictions.

item.description:
## Bookings

Students book sessions within a professor's availability window. Bookings start in `pending` status; the professor then confirms or cancels.

**Status transitions:**
- `pending` → `confirmed` (professor or admin)
- `pending` / `confirmed` → `cancelled` (student, professor, or admin)

**Booking rules:**
- Only students can create bookings.
- The student must be enrolled in the course the availability window belongs to.
- `start_time` and `end_time` must fall within the availability window.
- The number of active (non-cancelled) bookings must be below `max_students`.

---

### Example — student books a slot
```json
POST /bookings
{
  "availability_id": "{{availability_id}}"
}
```
**Response `201`:**
```json
{ "id": "...", "student_id": "...", "professor_id": "...", "course_id": "...", "availability_id": "...", "start_time": "...", "end_time": "...", "status": "pending", "created_at": "..." }
```

item.name: Chapters

request.description: Reorder the lectures within a chapter (admin). 204 on success.

item.description:
## Chapters

Sit inside a course and hold an ordered sequence of lectures (`position` controls order).

**Access control** mirrors Courses — `admin_only` for writes, enrollment-checked for reads on a specific `chapter_id` (resolved internally via `chapter.course_id`).

---

### Example 1 — Admin adds a chapter to a course
**Request:** `POST /chapters`
```json
{ "course_id": "{{course_id}}", "title": "Getting Started", "position": 0 }
```
**Response `201`:**
```json
{
  "id": "b2c3d4e5-...",
  "course_id": "018732f6-ae85-4cfc-ba46-e3e78a4291d8",
  "title": "Getting Started",
  "position": 0
}
```

### Example 2 — Reordering chapters
**Request:** `PATCH /chapters/{{chapter_id}}`
```json
{ "position": 2 }
```
Only the fields you send are updated — `title` is left untouched (`exclude_unset=True` on the server).

### Example 3 — Enrolled student views a chapter with its lectures
**Request:** `GET /chapters/{{chapter_id}}/detail`
**Response `200`:**
```json
{
  "id": "b2c3d4e5-...",
  "course_id": "018732f6-...",
  "title": "Getting Started",
  "position": 0,
  "lectures": [
    { "id": "c3d4e5f6-...", "title": "Variables and Data Types", "position": 0, "blocks": [], "exercises": [] }
  ]
}
```

### Example 4 — Listing chapters filtered by course
**Request:** `GET /chapters?course_id={{course_id}}`
Tick the disabled `course_id` query param checkbox in this request to activate the filter.

item.name: Lectures

request.description: Reorder the exercises within a lecture (admin). 204 on success.

item.description:
## Lectures

Belong to a chapter; hold ordered **blocks** (markdown content) and **exercises**.

**Access control:** writes are `admin_only`; reads on a specific `lecture_id` walk up to the parent chapter's course to check enrollment.

---

### Example 1 — Admin creates a lecture
**Request:** `POST /lectures`
```json
{ "chapter_id": "{{chapter_id}}", "title": "Variables and Data Types", "position": 0 }
```
**Response `201`:**
```json
{ "id": "c3d4e5f6-...", "chapter_id": "b2c3d4e5-...", "title": "Variables and Data Types", "position": 0 }
```

### Example 2 — Adding markdown content blocks
**Request:** `POST /lectures/{{lecture_id}}/blocks`
```json
{ "lecture_id": "{{lecture_id}}", "markdown": "## Introduction\n\nWelcome to this lecture.", "position": 0 }
```
Blocks render in order by `position` — add multiple blocks with increasing `position` values to build a lecture page.

### Example 3 — Full lecture detail (blocks + exercises in one call)
**Request:** `GET /lectures/{{lecture_id}}/detail`
**Response `200`:**
```json
{
  "id": "c3d4e5f6-...",
  "title": "Variables and Data Types",
  "blocks": [{ "id": "...", "markdown": "## Introduction...", "position": 0 }],
  "exercises": [{ "id": "...", "title": "FizzBuzz", "position": 0, "code_template": "..." }]
}
```

### Example 4 — Unenrolled student is blocked
**Request:** `GET /lectures/{{lecture_id}}` for a lecture in a course the student hasn't joined.
**Response `403`:** `{ "detail": "You are not enrolled in this course" }`

item.name: Exercises
item.description:
## Exercises

Belong to a lecture; hold instructional **blocks**, **test cases**, and a **code_template** that pre-fills the student's editor (e.g. C++ boilerplate or a Python function stub).

**Access control:** writes are `admin_only`; reads require enrollment in the exercise's parent course.

**Test cases drive grading.** Every `TestCase` row attached to an exercise (`input` + `expected_output`) is used by the Submissions flow: the student's program is run once per test case (sequentially) with `input` as stdin, and stdout is compared against `expected_output`. Execution stops at the first failure. See the **Submissions** folder for the full grading flow and the `passed_count`/`total_count` response fields.

---

### Example 1 — Admin creates an exercise with a C++ template
**Request:** `POST /exercises`
```json
{
  "lecture_id": "{{lecture_id}}",
  "title": "FizzBuzz",
  "position": 0,
  "code_template": "#include <iostream>\n\nint main() {\n    // your code here\n    return 0;\n}"
}
```

### Example 2 — Admin creates a Python exercise instead
```json
{
  "lecture_id": "{{lecture_id}}",
  "title": "Reverse a String",
  "position": 1,
  "code_template": "def reverse_string(s):\n    pass"
}
```
`code_template` is just a string — the client renders it as the starting point in the student's code editor.

### Example 3 — Adding test cases that will be used for grading
**Request:** `POST /exercises/{{exercise_id}}/test-cases`
```json
{ "exercise_id": "{{exercise_id}}", "input": "15", "expected_output": "FizzBuzz", "description": "Divisible by both 3 and 5" }
```
Add several test cases with different `input` values — each becomes a separate graded run when a student submits. Runs are sequential and stop at the first failure (see Submissions folder for full details).

### Example 4 — Student fetches the exercise to start working
**Request:** `GET /exercises/{{exercise_id}}`
**Response `200`:**
```json
{
  "id": "...",
  "lecture_id": "...",
  "title": "FizzBuzz",
  "position": 0,
  "code_template": "#include <iostream>..."
}
```

item.name: Submissions
item.description:
## Submissions — Remote Code Execution & Test Case Grading

Students submit code for an exercise; it's executed in an isolated Docker container on a separate runner VM, graded against the exercise's test cases, and the result is returned synchronously.

**How execution works:**
1. A `Submission` row is created with `status = queued`, then flipped to `running`
2. All `TestCase` rows for the exercise are fetched in order
3. The code is sent to the remote executor **one test case at a time** — each call is a single-element `/run-batch` request
4. Each run's stdout is compared (trimmed) against that test case's `expected_output`
5. **On the first failure** (wrong output, non-zero exit code, or timeout) the loop `break`s — no further test cases are executed
6. `passed_count` and `total_count` are stored on the submission; a `SubmissionTestResult` row is written for every test case that **was** run

**Grading result fields:**
- `passed_count` — integer count of test cases that passed (e.g. `17`)
- `total_count` — total test cases on the exercise (e.g. `36`)
- Display as `"17/36"` on the frontend
- Both are `null` when the exercise has no test cases
- `test_results` — array of per-test-case objects (only for test cases that were actually run, stopping at the first failure)

**`TestCaseResult` shape:**
```json
{
  "test_case_id": "uuid",
  "order_index": 0,
  "passed": true,
  "actual_output": "...",
  "stderr": "",
  "exit_code": "0",
  "timed_out": false
}
```

**Status logic:**
| Condition | `status` |
|---|---|
| All test cases passed | `passed` |
| First failure was a timeout | `timeout` |
| First failure was a non-zero exit code | `error` |
| First failure was wrong output (exit 0) | `failed` |

**No test cases on the exercise?** The submission still runs once (no stdin, no grading) — `passed_count`, `total_count`, and `test_results` are `null`/`[]`, and status is based on whether the program exited cleanly.

**Access control:** same `enrolled_for_exercise` guard as exercises — must be enrolled in the parent course. Students only see their own submissions; admins see everyone's.

**Supported languages:** `python`, `cpp`

---

### Example 1 — All test cases pass
**Request:** `POST /exercises/{{exercise_id}}/submissions`
```json
{ "code": "n = int(input())\nprint(n * 2)", "language": "python" }
```
**Response `201`:**
```json
{
  "id": "d4e5f6a7-...",
  "status": "passed",
  "passed_count": 3,
  "total_count": 3,
  "stdout": "10\n",
  "stderr": "",
  "exit_code": "0",
  "timed_out": false,
  "created_at": "2026-06-24T10:00:00Z",
  "test_results": [
    { "test_case_id": "...", "order_index": 0, "passed": true, "actual_output": "4\n",  "exit_code": "0", "timed_out": false },
    { "test_case_id": "...", "order_index": 1, "passed": true, "actual_output": "6\n",  "exit_code": "0", "timed_out": false },
    { "test_case_id": "...", "order_index": 2, "passed": true, "actual_output": "10\n", "exit_code": "0", "timed_out": false }
  ]
}
```
`stdout` reflects the **last** test case executed. `passed_count`/`total_count` give the fraction for the frontend.

### Example 2 — Early stop on first wrong answer
Buggy code passes test case 0, fails test case 1 (wrong output). Test cases 2–35 are **never executed**.
**Response `201`:**
```json
{
  "status": "failed",
  "passed_count": 1,
  "total_count": 36,
  "test_results": [
    { "order_index": 0, "passed": true,  "actual_output": "2\n" },
    { "order_index": 1, "passed": false, "actual_output": "wrong\n" }
  ]
}
```
Only 2 `test_results` rows exist in the DB — test cases 2–35 have no rows because execution stopped.

### Example 3 — Submission to an exercise WITH NO test cases
**Response `201`:**
```json
{ "status": "passed", "passed_count": null, "total_count": null, "test_results": [], "stdout": "Hello World\n", "exit_code": "0" }
```

### Example 4 — Compilation error (C++)
First test case fails with non-zero exit code → execution stops immediately.
**Response `201`:**
```json
{
  "status": "error",
  "passed_count": 0,
  "total_count": 36,
  "test_results": [
    { "order_index": 0, "passed": false, "actual_output": "", "stderr": "Compilation error:\n...", "exit_code": "1" }
  ]
}
```

### Example 5 — Timeout on first test case
**Response `201`:**
```json
{
  "status": "timeout",
  "passed_count": 0,
  "total_count": 36,
  "test_results": [
    { "order_index": 0, "passed": false, "timed_out": true, "exit_code": "124" }
  ]
}
```

### Example 6 — Submission history for an exercise
**Request:** `GET /exercises/{{exercise_id}}/submissions`
**Response `200`:**
```json
[
  { "id": "...", "status": "passed",  "passed_count": 36, "total_count": 36, "created_at": "2026-06-24T10:00:00Z", "test_results": [...] },
  { "id": "...", "status": "failed",  "passed_count": 1,  "total_count": 36, "created_at": "2026-06-24T09:55:00Z", "test_results": [...] },
  { "id": "...", "status": "timeout", "passed_count": 0,  "total_count": 36, "created_at": "2026-06-24T09:50:00Z", "test_results": [...] }
]
```
Ordered newest-first. `test_results` is included on every item — each list only contains the test cases that were actually run for that submission.

### Example 7 — Admin reviewing a specific attempt
**Request:** `GET /exercises/{{exercise_id}}/submissions/{{submission_id}}`
Admins can fetch **any** submission; a student fetching someone else's `submission_id` gets `403 Access denied`.

item.name: Submit C++ Solution (graded against test cases)

request.description: Submits C++ code that doubles its input. Test cases are run one at a time; execution stops on the first failure. Response includes `passed_count`/`total_count` integers (e.g. `3`/`36`) and a `test_results` array covering only the test cases that were actually executed.

item.name: Submit Python Solution (graded against test cases)

request.description: Reads an integer from stdin and prints FizzBuzz up to it. Pairs well with test cases that supply different `input` values (e.g. "5", "15", "3"). Each test case is run sequentially; the first wrong answer, crash, or timeout stops execution and no further test cases are run. The `submission_id` is auto-saved to the collection variable.

item.name: Submit Solution (no test cases on exercise)

request.description: Use this against an exercise that has ZERO test cases attached. The code runs exactly once with no stdin. `passed_count`, `total_count` will be `null` and `test_results` will be `[]` since there is nothing to grade against.

item.name: Submit Broken Code (test stderr / compile error)

request.description: Intentionally broken code. The first test case fails with a non-zero exit code, execution stops immediately. `passed_count` is 0, `status` is `error`, and `test_results` has exactly one entry (the failed first run).

Infinite loop — verifies `timed_out` is true and `exit_code` is '124'. The first test case times out, execution stops, and `test_results` has exactly one entry. `status` is `timeout`, `passed_count` is 0.
Students see only their own submissions ordered newest first. Each submission includes `passed_count`, `total_count`, and `test_results`. Admins see all submissions for the exercise.
Fetch a specific submission by ID. Response includes `passed_count`, `total_count`, `status`, `stdout`, `stderr`, `exit_code`, `timed_out`, and the full `test_results` array.
Grade code against the exercise's test cases and return the same result shape as a submission, persisting nothing (item #11).
